description: From the first job posting to the final paycheck, workplace decisions carry legal and ethical
consequences. Students examine employment law from the perspectives of managers, leaders, and
entrepreneurs. Topics include contractor status, hiring, wages, safety, leave, discrimination,
accommodations, discipline, and termination. Discussion-based sessions use realistic scenarios to
build analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills for organizational leadership. Offered
annually during spring semester. Prerequisite:  BUS 110 or permission of the instructor.
